title: NLP for Counterspeech against Hate: A Survey and How-To Guide
measurement_description: The paper surveys studies that measured and evaluated counterspeech against hate speech targeting religious groups (Jews, Muslims) and misinformation related to religious demographics. It also covers studies on classifying and generating counterspeech that might leverage religious identity (Christian affiliation) or address religious hypocrisy (Bible interpretations) in response to hate speech.
findings: The survey highlights that hate speech frequently targets religious groups such as Jews and Muslims. Counterspeech examples demonstrate strategies to address religious topics, including refuting religious stereotypes, offering alternative religious viewpoints (e.g., converting to Buddhism), leveraging personal religious affiliation (Christianity), and correcting misinformation linked to religious demographics (e.g., Muslim migrants). The paper also notes the presence of Islamophobia as a target of hate and the use of counterspeech to point out religious hypocrisy (e.g., interpretations of the Bible). It implicitly suggests that culturally and religiously specific responses are essential for effective hate speech mitigation.
